title: Rotate artifact annotations and enhance release manifest assembly for private installer CI
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Improve installer release manifest generation: rotate artifact-level annotations for provenance, add environment-tagged manifest fragments for safer rollbacks, and bump Helm chart schema for v0.18.0. No user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: our private-installer release pipeline currently stamps artifact provenance in a single monolithic annotations blob which makes incremental rollforward/rollback brittle in air-gapped environments. This PR splits per-artifact annotation blobs, rotates annotation keys for KMS-backed signing metadata, and introduces a small manifest fragment assembler that produces environment-tagged release manifests (e.g. vpc-staging, onprem-aws, onprem-baremetal).

Summary of changes: consolidated signing metadata serializer into scripts/signing/annotation_rotator.py; added a manifest fragment assembler at ci/release/manifest_fragments.go that merges signed shards into environment-specific release manifests; bumped helm/redwood-installer/Chart.yaml to apiVersion v2 and updated values schema for chart hooks used by upgrade/rollback; added Terraform module output to terraform/modules/installer/outputs.tf for release_manifest_ref to ease automation; added docs/docs/releases/manifest-rotation.md with operational runbook.

Why this is different: instead of rotating a single index, we now maintain per-artifact annotation files alongside the release index so the installer can apply or rollback individual components without re-signing unrelated artifacts. The annotation_rotator supports retention windows and key version tags so KMS/COSIGN rotations are decoupled from manifest assembly.

Testing: unit tests for annotation serializer and assembler integrated into CI; end-to-end pipeline run in staging created env-specific manifests and performed a dry-run install using the private-installer image. Verified artifact apply/rollback by toggling a single service manifest. See CI logs linked below.

Rollout plan: merge to main; the release job will publish a v0.18.0-installer candidate to the internal bucket and publish environment-tagged manifests. Staged rollout to vpc-staging for 48h, then to onprem-aws. If anything fails, the manifest assembler supports a --rebuild=false mode to re-use last consistent fragments and we can perform immediate rollback by selecting the previous fragment tag.

Notes: this PR touches signing utilities and release assembly; ops must have KMS key version available in staging before the next roll. Linear ENG-1972 contains the automated optional fallback to previous-key when cosign verification fails.

Small illustrative snippet (annotation_rotator usage):
  $ python3 scripts/signing/annotation_rotator.py --key-version v2 --source-bucket releases/staging/2025-11-03 --out-prefix fragments/vpc-staging

Files of interest (high-level): ci/release/manifest_fragments.go, scripts/signing/annotation_rotator.py, helm/redwood-installer/Chart.yaml, terraform/modules/installer/outputs.tf, docs/releases/manifest-rotation.md
